question: If the simple interest on a certain sum of money for 4 years at 5% per annum is ₹500, what would be the simple interest on the same sum for 6 years at 7% per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the Principal is constant, Simple Interest (SI) is directly proportional to (Rate × Time).

Effective Rate percentage for Case 1 = 5% × 4 = 20%

Effective Rate percentage for Case 2 = 7% × 6 = 42%

Since 20% corresponds to ₹500, then 42% will correspond to (500 ÷ 20) × 42.

New Simple Interest = 25 × 42 = ₹1050.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SI₁ = ₹500

T₁ = 4 years, R₁ = 5% per annum

T₂ = 6 years, R₂ = 7% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Principal (P)
 
 
• 
 4 years @ 5% p.a.
 R × T = 20%

 
 SI = ₹500

 
 Principal (P)

 
• 
 6 years @ 7% p.a.
 R × T = 42%

 
 SI = ₹1050

**Calculation:**

Using the given data for Case 1 to find the Principal (P):

⇒ 500 = (P × 5 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 500 = (P × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (500 × 100) ÷ 20

⇒ P = ₹2500

Now, finding the Simple Interest for Case 2 using the same Principal:

⇒ SI₂ = (2500 × 7 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 25 × 42

⇒ SI₂ = ₹1050

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality of Simple Interest

When the principal amount is kept constant, simple interest becomes strictly proportional to the product of Rate (R) and Time (T). Formula ratio form: SI₁ ÷ SI₂ = (R₁ × T₁) ÷ (R₂ × T₂).

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) after simple interest is accrued is given by A = P + SI = P(1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

For any given principal P and rate R% per annum, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest strictly for a 2-year period is D = P(R ÷ 100)².
